How to Analyze Banks (Part 2): Deposits, Valuations, and Silicon Valley

Eisman explains deposit franchises, SVB's duration and funding failure, bank income statements and tangible-book valuation. He favors large banks but avoids adding them at rich valuations and with AI financing exposure. The central SVB mechanism and conditional arithmetic are useful. Material errors concern securities accounting, liquidity-rule maturity restrictions, SVB closure timing and OZK consumer lending. Current credit data is broadly stable, but not uniformly benign. Claims of zero systemic risk and inevitable consolidation are substantially less established.

Substack · 2026-09-23 ↗
A useful bank-analysis framework with several consequential factual and accounting simplifications. Distinguish book, regulatory and economic capital; liquidity from duration; and reported returns from stock-valuation judgments. The solo presentation means all extracted substantive views are Eisman's.

  • SVB and SIVB refer to bank and holding-company ticker; their asset totals and capital measures differ.

  • The spoken flat/nonaccrual generalization does not include a bank-by-bank data table in the transcript.

substack-216147653-c014 · explanation

Mixed
Source · 7:32-8:46 ↗
SpeakerSteve Eisman
Stanceconditional
Horizonnot stated
Materialitymajor

Holding avoids crystallizing a market discount if payments arrive; stability alone does not remove economic capital loss, negative carry or every solvency risk.

Conditional reasoning

Assume contractual bond payments are made, deposits remain available through maturity, and all other cash obligations can be met. With no required sale, the bank collects contractual principal and coupons rather than selling at the lower market price. However, present value still falls when the discount rate rises, and stable deposits alone do not prove the other liquidity or solvency assumptions. Thus the conditional funding insight is valid but incomplete as a general solvency claim.

Assessment test: Evaluate funding persistence, capital, collateral capacity and contractual repayment.

Evidence and assessment details

Attribution confidence: high. Assessment confidence: medium. Thesis family: bank-liquidity.

How he reasons here

  • Analyze deposit composition and correlation, not merely total balances.
  • Separate funding cost, asset duration and credit risk.
  • Decompose pre-provision earnings from credit provisions.
  • Compare tangible-book multiples with sustainable returns and cost of equity.
  • Treat good valuation logic as insufficient to predict merger execution.
  • Assess indirect portfolio exposure through investment-banking clients.
